text:
sam: Heads-up — enterprise POC: tool-calls returning JSON but required numeric fields sometimes show up as null or as odd placeholders ("N/A", "—"). Customer says it happens ~10% of runs. Demo in 24h, needs triage.

maria: can we get a raw example of the response? also which API flags are they using (json_mode/strict_fn_calls/streaming)?

sam: posted an example to the ticket: ```{\"tool\":\"order_parser\",\"fn\":\"extract_order\",\"args\":{\"order_id\":\"12345\",\"amount\":\"N/A\",\"currency\":\"USD\"}}``` they run with json_mode=strict + streaming=true.

devin: interesting — if streaming is enabled we sometimes cut output mid-structure and our strict serializer interprets missing numeric tokens as null after coercion. have we seen similar for this customer before?

sam: not before. they also report intermittent TLS timeout errors from their egress proxy during the same timeframe.

lee: two parallel tracks: 1) parsing robustness: quick fixes: a) disable strict coercion for the POC (fall back to tolerant parsing), b) add an explicit end-of-json marker in the prompt (e.g. "\n<END_JSON>"), c) require the model to wrap the JSON in a json code fence. all low-friction.

maria: for the longer-term, suggest enabling a post-response normalization step: map common placeholders ("N/A","—","NaN") to null or to zero depending on schema rules, then validate and surface mismatches to the customer. note this shouldn't be live default for all customers.

ops-bot: [connector] 1749501155 WARN connection: tls_handshake_timeout from customer-proxy-ip, err="alert handshake failure"; retry backoff engaged.

security-bot: TLS error often means their proxy is terminating TLS for inspection. ask them to provide proxy logs and cert chain. if they cannot change appliance, recommend TLS passthrough or adding our CA to the appliance trust store for demo.

devin: another angle: check if the client sent an explicit charset header. we had a case where an upstream changed charset to "utf-16" and our byte-level scanners misaligned braces. also check for stray BOMs.

sam: customer is on a Windows service that outsources parsing to an in-house ETL that may emit weird characters. i'll ask them to sample raw_response base64.

maria: also try a model-side tweak: reduce max_output_tokens slightly and add a short "finish" sentence that is the sentinel. sometimes that prevents the model from appending extra commentary that breaks strict parsing.

devin: if they're using r-infer-2-medium try toggling to non-streaming for the POC run — increases latency slightly but often eliminates mid-object truncation. for scaling, we can automate re-requests when bracket mismatch is detected.

lee: quick engineering plan for the POC: A) deploy a temporary tolerant JSON extractor that performs bracket matching and strips trailing garbage, B) add normalization for placeholder values, C) revert to strict mode after we ship proper fix. estimate: 1 dev-day + QA.

security-bot: for the TLS path: propose doc snippets for customer security: (1) whitelist outbound CIDR ranges, (2) configure passthrough for our endpoints, or (3) import our intermediate cert. which do they prefer?

sam: i'll surface options and ask for proxy logs. pricing note from the customer: they worry retries/longer outputs will increase token cost. how should we position?

maria: frame it as a demo-stabilization cost: small incremental token usage for demo traffic; propose a waived overage for the week of demo (sales decision). engineering can provide token estimate based on sample QPS.

devin: small tip: when numeric fields are the issue, sometimes the model emits numbers as words ("one hundred") — our coercer fails and returns null. consider adding a numeric-normalizer step that attempts int/float parsing of common word patterns.

lee: i'll spin up a hotfix branch for the tolerant extractor and drop a feature flag so we can toggle quickly.

sam: thanks — please keep the ticket updated. customer asked for an ETA for a fix before the demo: can we commit to the 1 dev-day hotfix?
maria: yes for the hotfix and the guidance for TLS options. will follow up with sales-runnote to propose temporary credits if needed.

sam: perfect. will collect raw_response and proxy logs and post back. ping me when the feature flag is ready.

ops-bot: action created: HOTFIX-4321 tolerant-json-extractor assigned to lee, due 24h.

maria: tagging legal/security in the ticket for guidance on cert distribution.

sam: closing loop here — thanks team, we'll keep momentum and aim to stabilize before demo.
